nodes.notes: Enrolment-time audit row. The dashboard's Campaigns screen builds its roster from the OLDEST audit_log row per lead_email, so without this row nobody shows as enrolled for seven days and then appears the moment the sequence has already ended. In series before 'Wait Day 1', not fanned out from it, so the row is written before the execution suspends.

nodes.name: Comm Keys (Day 1)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (() => { const pick = (n, f) => { try { const v = ($(n).first().json || {})[f]; return v ? String(v).trim() : null; } catch (e) { return null; } }; const em = pick('Lead State (Day 1)', 'email') || pick('Normalize Lead Input', 'email') || ''; const ph = pick('Lead State (Day 1)', 'phone') || pick('Normalize Lead Input', 'phone') || ''; return JSON.stringify({ p_email: em, p_phone: ph }); })() }}

nodes.notes: Added 30 Aug 2026 (dripid regression fix). Resolves EVERY spelling of this lead's address that communication_logs.lead_email could hold, by calling the live Postgres function nexus_comm_keys_for_lead(p_email, p_phone) -- the same key set the 12-Hour Silence Detector and Fetch Thread History use. It is the only resolver that can see '<opaque>@lid' chat ids, because a LID carries no phone digits and can only be reached by joining whatsapp_contacts (chat_id -> phone / lead_email), which the function does server-side. TODAY 51 of 91 communication_logs rows are @lid and ZERO are @c.us, so without this node the gate downstream is nearly blind. responseFormat is 'text' ON PURPOSE: the RPC returns a JSON array and an HTTP node splits an array response into one item PER ELEMENT, which would run every node after it once per key. Text keeps it to one item; the consumer JSON.parse()s it. onError=continueRegularOutput: if the RPC is unreachable the gate falls back to the locally derived keys (email + digit forms) and behaves exactly as it did before this fix -- never worse. One node PER GATE, not one shared node: whatsapp_contacts gains a row the moment a customer first messages from a LID chat, so a key set snapshotted on day 1 would not contain the day-5 reply we exist to detect.

nodes.notes: Enrolment-time audit row. nodes.name: Comm Keys (Day 1)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (() => { const pick = (n, f) => { try { const v = ($(n).first().json || {})[f]; return v ? String(v).trim() : null; } catch (e) { return null; } }; const em = pick('Lead State (Day 1)', 'email') || pick('Normalize Lead Input', 'email') || ''; const ph = pick('Lead State (Day 1)', 'phone') || pick('Normalize Lead Input', 'phone') || ''; return JSON.stringify({ p_email: em, p_phone: ph }); })() }}

nodes.notes: Added 30 Aug 2026 (dripid regression fix). Resolves EVERY spelling of this lead's address that communication_logs.lead_email could hold, by calling the live Postgres function nexus_comm_keys_for_lead(p_email, p_phone) -- the same key set the 12-Hour Silence Detector and Fetch Thread History use. It is the only resolver that can see '<opaque>@lid' chat ids, because a LID carries no phone digits and can only be reached by joining whatsapp_contacts (chat_id -> phone / lead_email), which the function does server-side. TODAY 51 of 91 communication_logs rows are @lid and ZERO are @c.us, so without this node the gate downstream is nearly blind. responseFormat is 'text' ON PURPOSE: the RPC returns a JSON array and an HTTP node splits an array response into one item PER ELEMENT, which would run every node after it once per key. Text keeps it to one item; the consumer JSON.parse()s it. onError=continueRegularOutput: if the RPC is unreachable the gate falls back to the locally derived keys (email + digit forms) and behaves exactly as it did before this fix -- never worse. One node PER GATE, not one shared node: whatsapp_contacts gains a row the moment a customer first messages from a LID chat, so a key set snapshotted on day 1 would not contain the day-5 reply we exist to detect.

activeVersion.name: Tenant-precedence: add JWT tenant lookup, harden resolver
activeVersion.description: Adds 'Tenant For JWT User' between Verify JWT and Normalize Lead Input on the public webhook door, and hardens Resolve Tenant / Normalize Lead Input so a verified user's tenant_members row is authoritative and a caller-supplied tenant_id claim is only ever cross-checked, never trusted. Part of the tenant-precedence wave.
